### How this work is cited

Passages inside Pensées are identified by fragment number — which numbering must be named. There is no single canonical numbering. The Brunschvicg (1897) and Lafuma (1951) systems differ, and a fragment number is meaningless without saying which it follows — a point the corpus flags where it records 'common numbering'. Pascal died before arranging the material, so the order of the fragments is editorial throughout.

### The work in Blaise Pascal’s thought

Blaise Pascal (1623–1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, and Christian apologist who invented an early calculator and advanced probability and fluid mechanics. After a decisive religious conversion, he defended Jansenism in the Provincial Letters and left unfinished Pensées. [More on Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) .
